newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ budget on track, savings to be extended - Peters.
newsitem.headline: NZ budget on track, savings to be extended - Peters.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters said on Tuesday that revenue and expenditure forecasts were very close to levels forecast in December, but that he would seek new fiscal savings after the June 26 budget.

He told an Institute of Management breakfast meeting that Wednesday's current year fiscal update would show "there is no government spending blowout" and "revenue and expenditure forecasts are very close to levels forecast in December".
"While working on the current budget we have realised we need still more savings, and following the budget we will work methodically through departments to find them," he added.
Peters gave no further details of these plans.
In general comments on the budget Peters said it would "spend the money as promised, but at the same time remain within the bounds set by the coalition agreement".

He also commented on the profusion of recent local press speculation that there are fractures within the centre-right coalition formed late last year by Peters' New Zealand First Party and the National Party.
"In short, the economy is in sound shape and so is the coalition government. I urge you all to not always believe what you read and hear in the media about us.
"We are here for the next three years. The June budget will well and truly get this coalition's agenda up and running," he said.
